title: Lester's family band, and his belief Smith gave him hard arrangements
summary: Smith recalls Lester's carnival family band and says Lester later told him he'd given him a hard time with the reed choruses.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Back to Lester Young again. I have a few little questions about him. We talked about the reeds; I got that down. Lester's early life. Did you ever run into Lester before you played with him?
No.
You had no idea what that little band was like that his family had. His father had a band.
No. All I knew is that his father used to have him on the carnival, because they used to follow a carnival around. And he had all his children that could play music...
He had sisters in there, right?
Buster Smith - 80
Yeah. He had a brother named Lee.
He's still around.
Yeah. He was a drummer, wasn't he.
I think he's still alive.
Is he?
I think so.
I haven't heard him in years.
Did Lester know that he was very, very good? Did he think of himself as being very, very good?
No, he didn't think so. I don't think so.
Really?
No, he didn't play that... He didn't have that kind of attitude. He was just trying to make it. I didn't know it, though, but he thought I was trying to stick him on these arrangements.
You mean...?
Yeah. I'd write arrangement that had them reed choruses and things like that. He thought I was trying to stick him with all that....
You mean trying to give him stuff he couldn't read?

Yeah, I think he did. I didn't recognize it, but he didn't make himself known on that until later years. He came down here with Basie. He wasn't in Basie's band, but he was added...him and Dizzy Gillespie was added attraction to Basie's
Buster Smith - 81

band. I think that was back in the late 50's... Yeah, it was around there. Just a little before the 60's, Billy Eckstine was with Basie, and they had come down through here. And Lester came out and said, "You give me a hard time." We grabbed each other and was rasslin'around out there in the back of the dance hall. We got through talking and everything, and I said, "Man, I'm glad for you." So Basie eased up to me, and told me, "Man, he doesn't blow his top(?). That cat there, he's something else." I said, "What's the matter with him?" He said, "I don't know." That's what he said. But I didn't know he was thinking that I was trying to stick him with the music.
That's not true.

Yeah. I was writing music, trying to make the band sound good. Eddie Durham... Wasn't but two arrangers in the band, Eddie Durham and myself, when we was with Bennie Moten. And Eddie Durham would write all those stiff choruses, reed choruses and things...
